questions.question: Which of the following methods is used to create a new folder in Windows 11 OS from Desktop?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Right-click → Select New → Folder**__

__
 
• To create a **new folder** in **Windows 11 OS** from the desktop, you can use the **context menu** by right-clicking.
 
• When you **right-click** on an empty space on the desktop, a menu appears with various options.
 
• Selecting the **"New"** option from the menu expands another sub-menu.
 
• In the sub-menu, choose **"Folder"**, which automatically creates a new folder on the desktop.
 
• The newly created folder appears with the default name **"New Folder"**, which can be renamed by typing a desired name immediately or later.
 
• This method is widely used as it is **quick and user-friendly**.
 
• It does not require any additional software or shortcuts, making it ideal for users of all **skill levels**.
 
• The functionality is consistent across various versions of Windows, including **Windows 10** and **Windows 11**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Press Alt + F4**__

 __
 
• The **Alt + F4** shortcut is used to **close the active window or application** in Windows.
 
• This shortcut does not create a new folder and serves a different purpose related to window management.
 
 
 
• **Drag a file to Desktop**__
 __
 
• Dragging a file to the desktop does not create a new folder but **moves or copies the selected file** to the desktop.
 
• This action is used for file organization rather than folder creation.
 
 
 
• **Press Ctrl + N**__
 
 
• **Ctrl + N** is commonly used to create a **new document or window** in applications like Microsoft Word or web browsers.
 
• This shortcut does not work for creating a folder on the desktop in Windows OS.

questions.question: Which of the following caves are famous for its high citadel?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Junagadh caves**__.

__
 
• The **Junagadh caves** are a group of Buddhist caves located in the **Junagadh district of Gujarat, India**.
 
• These caves are famous for their **high citadel** and architectural significance.
 
• The caves are divided into three main groups: **Uparkot caves, Khapra Kodiya caves,** and the **Baba Pyare caves**.
 
• They were primarily used as **monasteries and meditation centers** by Buddhist monks during the 2nd to 4th centuries CE.
 
• The caves are adorned with **pillars, water tanks, and prayer halls**, reflecting the influence of Buddhist rock-cut architecture.
 
• The **Uparkot caves**, in particular, are known for their location within a high citadel, offering panoramic views of the surroundings.
 
• The intricate carvings and structural designs of the caves showcase the advanced techniques of ancient Indian craftsmen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sudama caves**__

 __
 
• The **Sudama caves** are part of the Barabar caves, located in **Bihar, India**.
 
• These caves are the **earliest examples of rock-cut architecture** in India and were used by the Ajivika sect.
 
• The caves were carved during the reign of Emperor **Ashoka** in the 3rd century BCE and are known for their **polished interior surfaces**.
 
 
 
• **Ellora caves**__
 __
 
• The **Ellora caves** are a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in **Maharashtra, India**.
 
• They represent a mix of **Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain** religious traditions.
 
• The caves are renowned for the **Kailasa temple**, a monolithic rock-cut structure dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Bagh caves**__
 
 
• The **Bagh caves** are located in the **Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh, India**.
 
• These caves are famous for their **ancient mural paintings**, which reflect Indian art from the Gupta period.
 
• They are associated with Buddhist monks who used them as **viharas (monasteries)**.

questions.question: The enactment of the first Cooperative Credit Societies Act in 1904 was influenced by which of the following?

• The commission highlighted the importance of establishing rural credit institutions to help farmers during times of distress.
 
• The recommendations of the Indian Famine Commission influenced the enactment of the **Cooperative Credit Societies Act of 1904**, which aimed to provide affordable credit to farmers and prevent exploitation by moneylenders.
 
• The act was a landmark step in the development of **cooperative movements in India**, especially in rural areas.
 
• It laid the foundation for the establishment of **cooperative societies**, which were designed to provide credit at reasonable rates and improve the financial stability of farmers.
 
• The initiative was crucial for addressing the agricultural distress caused by recurring famines and boosting rural development.

 __
 
• The **Royal Commission on Agriculture** was set up in **1926** to study agricultural issues in India and recommend solutions for improving the agrarian economy.
 
• Its recommendations were more focused on **land tenure systems, irrigation, marketing, and agricultural practices**, rather than rural credit.
 
 
 
• **Hunter Commission**__
 __
 
• The **Hunter Commission**, established in **1882**, dealt with **education reforms** in India and had no direct connection to agricultural credit or the Cooperative Credit Societies Act.
 
• It primarily focused on expanding and improving **primary and secondary education** in India.
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission**__

questions.question: Who administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Union Ministers under Article 75(4) of the Constitution of India?

__
 
• Under **Article 75(4) of the Constitution of India**, the oath of office and secrecy is administered to the Union Ministers by the **President of India.**
 
• The oath is taken in accordance with the provisions of the **Third Schedule** of the Constitution.
 
• The President ensures that the Union Ministers pledge to uphold the **Constitution of India**, maintain secrecy, and perform their duties faithfully.
 
• The President is the head of the state and serves as the **constitutional authority** responsible for appointing Union Ministers as per the advice of the **Prime Minister.**
 
• This process reflects the principle of maintaining the integrity and solemnity of the **parliamentary democracy** in India.

__

 __
 
• The **Chief Justice of India (CJI)** primarily heads the judiciary and does not administer the oath of office and secrecy to Union Ministers.
 
• The Chief Justice is responsible for interpreting the Constitution and overseeing the functioning of the **Supreme Court of India.**
 
• However, the CJI administers the oath to the **President of India and Governors** in specific circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister**__
 __
 
• The **Prime Minister** acts as the head of the government and advises the President on the appointment of Union Ministers.
 
• While the Prime Minister plays a significant role in governance, he/she does not administer the oath to Union Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Vice President**__
 
 
• The **Vice President of India** is primarily responsible for officiating in the absence of the President and serves as the Chairman of the **Rajya Sabha.**
 
• The Vice President does not have the constitutional authority to administer the oath to Union Ministers.

questions.question: With whose assistance did Chandragupta Maurya overthrow the Nanda dynasty?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Chanakya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chanakya**, also known as **Kautilya** or **Vishnugupta**, was a renowned ancient Indian philosopher, economist, and statesman.
 
• He played a pivotal role in assisting **Chandragupta Maurya** in overthrowing the **Nanda dynasty** and establishing the **Maurya Empire**.
 
• Chanakya is credited with authoring the **Arthashastra**, an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
 
• He was a master strategist who used his knowledge and wit to mentor Chandragupta Maurya and unite the fragmented regions of India under a single empire.
 
• Chanakya’s guidance was instrumental in planning and executing the strategies to defeat the Nandas, who were powerful rulers at the time.
 
• Chanakya’s contributions to Indian political thought and governance are considered pioneering and are still studied widely.
 
• He is often referred to as the “**Machiavelli of India**” for his diplomatic and political acumen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Megasthenes**__

 __
 
• **Megasthenes** was a Greek ambassador to the Mauryan court during the reign of **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• He authored the book **Indica**, which provides insights into the Mauryan Empire and ancient Indian society.
 
• However, he did not play any role in the overthrow of the Nanda dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Bindusara**__
 __
 
• **Bindusara** was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and the second ruler of the Maurya Empire.
 
• He succeeded Chandragupta and expanded the empire further but was not involved in the overthrow of the Nandas.
 
 
 
• **Bimbisara**__
 
 
• **Bimbisara** was a ruler of the **Haryanka dynasty** in ancient India and a contemporary of the Buddha.
 
• He ruled the kingdom of Magadha but lived long before Chandragupta and Chanakya.

questions.question: Which provision was introduced in the Constitution of India through the 74th Amendment Act?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Part IX-A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **74th Amendment Act** of the Indian Constitution, enacted in **1992**, specifically introduced **Part IX-A**, which deals with the governance of **urban local bodies**.
 
• This amendment provides a **constitutional status** to urban local self-governments such as **Municipal Corporations, Municipalities, and Nagar Panchayats**.
 
• It aims to ensure **decentralization** in urban governance and encourage **grassroots democracy** in urban areas.
 
• **Article 243-P to Article 243-ZG** were added to the Constitution under Part IX-A, detailing the **composition, powers, and responsibilities** of urban local bodies.
 
• It mandates the establishment of **Ward Committees** in municipalities with a population of over **3 lakh**, ensuring greater **citizen participation**.
 
• The amendment also outlines provisions for the **reservation of seats** for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women in urban local bodies.
 
• A **State Finance Commission** is to be constituted to recommend measures for the financial health of these bodies.
 
• The 74th Amendment is significant for promoting **good governance** and addressing the challenges of **urbanization** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Part X**__

 __
 
• **Part X** of the Constitution deals with the **Scheduled and Tribal Areas**.
 
• It includes provisions for the administration and governance of these areas to protect the interests of **Scheduled Tribes**.
 
• It covers **Articles 244 and 244A**.
 
 
 
• **Part IX**__
 __
 
• **Part IX** of the Constitution deals with **Panchayati Raj Institutions** and was added through the **73rd Amendment Act, 1992**.
 
• It focuses on **rural local governance** and includes **Articles 243 to 243-O**.
 
 
 
• **Part XI**__
 
 
• **Part XI** of the Constitution deals with the **relations between the Union and the States**.
 
• It includes provisions related to **legislative and administrative relations**, covered under **Articles 245 to 263**.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Lord Thomas Babington Macaulay** was a British historian, politician, and lawmaker who played a pivotal role in shaping the administrative and educational policies of **British India**.
 
• He is best known for drafting the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)**, which became the backbone of the Indian legal system and is still in use today with modifications.
 
• The IPC was a comprehensive code of criminal law for India, and it was officially enacted in **1860**.
 
• In addition to his work on the IPC, Macaulay strongly advocated for the promotion of **English education in India**.
 
• His famous **"Minute on Education"** (1835) laid the foundation for the use of English as the medium of instruction in Indian schools and colleges.
 
• Macaulay believed that English education would create a class of Indians who were **"Indian in blood and color, but English in taste, in opinions, in morals, and in intellect."**
 
• His efforts significantly influenced the spread of Western education, science, and literature in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Framing the Government of India Act, 1858**__

 __
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1858** marked the formal transfer of power from the **East India Company** to the British Crown.
 
• This Act was introduced after the **Indian Rebellion of 1857** to improve governance in India.
 
• However, Macaulay was not directly involved in drafting this Act.
 
 
 
• **Introducing the Vernacular Press Act**__
 __
 
• The **Vernacular Press Act** of 1878 was introduced by **Lord Lytton**, not Macaulay.
 
• This Act aimed to curb the freedom of the Indian-language press and suppress criticism of British policies.
 
 
 
• **Leading the revolt of 1857**__
 
 
• The **Indian Rebellion of 1857** was a large-scale uprising against British rule, but Macaulay was not involved in leading it.
 
• By the time of the revolt, Macaulay had already returned to England and was not in India.

questions.question: In industrial settings, Freon-12 is most commonly manufactured by which chemical reaction?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Swarts reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swarts reaction** is a method for the preparation of haloalkanes, particularly fluorinated compounds.
 
• In this reaction, **metal fluorides** like AgF, SbF3, or Hg2F2 are used to replace halogens (chlorine or bromine) in alkyl halides.
 
• Freon-12 (**Dichlorodifluoromethane**) is commonly prepared using the Swarts reaction as it involves the replacement of chlorine atoms in chlorinated hydrocarbons with fluorine atoms.
 
• The reaction is widely applied in the **industrial production of Freon compounds**, which are used as refrigerants.
 
• Freon-12 has been extensively utilized in **air conditioning and refrigeration systems** due to its physical properties, such as low boiling point and non-flammability.
 
• However, its use has been phased out in many countries due to its **ozone-depleting potential** under the Montreal Protocol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Substitution reaction**__

 __
 
• In a substitution reaction, one atom or group in a molecule is replaced by another atom or group.
 
• It is a common reaction in organic chemistry and involves mechanisms like **SN1 and SN2 reactions**.
 
• While substitution reactions are used for synthesizing various compounds, they are not the primary method for producing fluorinated hydrocarbons like Freon-12.
 
 
 
• **Wurtz reaction**__
 __
 
• The Wurtz reaction is a method used to prepare higher alkanes by reacting alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether.
 
• This reaction is not suitable for the production of fluorinated hydrocarbons like Freon-12.
 
 
 
• **Elimination reaction**__
 
 
• Elimination reactions involve the removal of atoms or groups from a molecule, resulting in the formation of double or triple bonds.
 
• These reactions do not involve the direct substitution of halogens with fluorine and are unrelated to the synthesis of Freon compounds.

• The **Shillong Plateau** is a significant geographical feature located in the northeastern part of India.
 
• It is primarily divided into three distinct regions: the **Khasi Hills**, **Jaintia Hills**, and **Garo Hills**.

• This case established the principle that the **Supreme Court of the United States** has the authority to review and invalidate laws and actions of the executive and legislative branches if they conflict with the **U.S. Constitution**.
 
• Judicial review is considered a fundamental aspect of the **separation of powers** and ensures that no branch of government exceeds its constitutional limits.

• **India**__

questions.question: What defines a conjoint vascular bundle?

options.text: Xylem and phloem alternate along the radii

__
 
• A **conjoint vascular bundle** is a type of vascular bundle where both **xylem** and **phloem** are present together on the same radius of the stem or root.
 
• It is a characteristic feature of most **angiosperms** and is commonly found in **dicot stems** and **monocot stems**.
 
• In this type of arrangement, the **xylem** is typically located towards the inner side (adaxial side), while the **phloem** is positioned towards the outer side (abaxial side).
 
• Conjoint vascular bundles are further classified into two types:
 
 
• **Collateral**: Xylem and phloem are present side by side in the same bundle (e.g., sunflower stem).
 
• **Bicollateral**: Xylem is sandwiched between two layers of phloem (e.g., Cucurbita stem).
 
 
 
• In most cases, conjoint vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of **parenchyma cells**, which form the vascular cambium in dicots.
 
• This arrangement is efficient for the transport of **water**, **minerals**, and **organic nutrients** throughout the plant body.

• Radial vascular bundles are found in **roots** of both monocots and dicots.
 
 
 
• **Xylem only on the outer side**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because xylem is usually located on the inner side in a conjoint vascular bundle.
 
• However, in **open vascular bundles**, the cambium allows for secondary growth, leading to the formation of additional xylem on the inside.
 
 
 
• **Cambium is absent**__
 
 
• This condition is seen in **closed vascular bundles**, which are common in **monocots**.
 
• In such bundles, there is no cambium, so secondary growth does not occur.

• Today, **Odissi** is performed globally and remains a significant part of India's cultural heritage.
